 1                    I.      INTRODUCTION AND QUALIFICATIONS

 2   Q1.   PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME, BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 3   A.    My name is Manuel Carrasco. My business address is 100 North Stanton Street,

 4         El Paso, Texas, 79901.

 5

 6   Q2.   ON WHOSE BEHALF ARE YOU SUBMITTING THIS TESTIMONY

 7   A.    I am filing this testimony on behalf of El Paso Electric Company (“EPE” or “the

 8         Company”).

 9

10   Q3.   HAVE YOU PREVIOUSLY SUBMITTED TESTIMONY IN THIS

11         PROCEEDING?

12   A.    Yes. I submitted Direct Testimony in this proceeding on March 27, 2026.

13

 4   Q5.   WHAT HAS THE COMMISSION REQUESTED IN PARAGRAPHS 9.b.i

 5         AND 9.b.ii OF THE PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST?

 6   A.    Paragraphs 9.b.i and 9.b.ii of the Pre-Hearing Bench Request request that EPE

 7         provide for (a) each class of service, (b) separately for the summer and non-summer

 8         months, and (c) for various levels of use, the following:

 9         •      Paragraph 9.b.i “The monthly bill under current rates stating separately the

10                customer charge, usage charge, any demand charge, the Fuel and Purchased

11                Power Cost Adjustment Clause (FPPCAC) charge, any other separate charges

12                (such as the renewable energy and energy efficiency rider charges) but

13                excluding taxes and surcharges and the total bill.”

14         •      Paragraph 9.b.ii “The monthly bill under proposed rates separately stating the

15                customer charge, usage charge, any demand charge, the FPPCAC charge, any

16                other separate charges (such as the renewable energy and energy efficiency

17                rider charges) but excluding taxes and surcharges and the total bill.”

18

19               “standard” rates;

15   Q8.   WHAT HAS THE COMMISSION REQUESTED IN PARAGRAPH 9.f OF

16         THE PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST?

17   A.    Paragraph 9.f of the Pre-Hearing Bench Request requests “…the base cost of fuel

18         (per kWh) incorporated into EPE’s existing rates.”

19

 1   Q9.   IN RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.f, WHAT IS THE BASE COST OF

 2         FUEL (PER kWh) INCORPORATED INTO EPE’S EXISTING RATES?

 3   A.    None. Pursuant to the Commission’s Final Order in Case No. 15-00127-UT, the

 4         Company was required to remove all fuel and purchased power costs from base

 5         rates and bill such costs through the Fuel and Purchased Power Cost Adjustment

 6         Clause (“FPPCAC”).

 7   Q10. WHAT HAS THE COMMISSION REQUESTED IN PARAGRAPH 9.g OF

8          THE PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST?

 9   A.    Paragraph 9.g of the Pre-Hearing Bench Request requests “…the base cost of fuel

10         incorporated into EPE’s proposed rates? Provide the dollar cost of fuel for the test

11         year and the billing units expressed in kWh used to determine the base cost of fuel.”

12

13   Q11. IN RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.g, WHAT IS THE BASE COST OF

14         FUEL INCORPORATED INTO EPE’S PROPOSED RATES? PROVIDE

15         THE DOLLAR COST OF FUEL FOR THE TEST YEAR AND THE

16         BILLING UNITS EXPRESSED IN kWh USED TO DETERMINE BASE

17         COST OF FUEL.

18   A.    None. Please see EPE’s response to paragraph 9.f above.

19

 1   Q12. WHAT HAS THE COMMISSION REQUESTED IN PARAGRAPH 9.h OF

 2        THE PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST?

 3   A.   Paragraph 9.h of the Pre-Hearing Bench Request requests “If EPE were to collect

 4        all of its fuel costs through base rates, what would be the base cost of fuel

 5        incorporated into the new rates proposed to take effect on January 1, 2027, and

 6        subsequently on October 1, 2027 (or whenever the proposed rates become

 7        effective)?”

 8   Q13. IN RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.h, PROVIDE THE BASE COST OF

 9        FUEL INCORPORATED INTO THE NEW RATES PROPOSED TO TAKE

10        EFFECT ON JANUARY 1, 2027, AND SUBSEQUENTLY ON OCTOBER 1,

11        2027, IF EPE WERE TO COLLECT ALL ITS FUEL COSTS THROUGH

12        BASE RATES.

13   A.   EPE is not proposing to incorporate fuel costs into any of the rates proposed in this

14        proceeding. For illustrative purposes only, Exhibit MC-1S at lines 19 through 23

15        column (d) provides the “base cost of fuel” that could be incorporated into base

16        rates, which is about one cent per kWh. Because the Final Order in Case No. 15-

17        00127-UT required EPE to remove all fuel and purchased power costs from base

18        rates, the calculations may not include all the details would have been necessary to

19        develop an accurate base cost of fuel rate.

 2   Q14. WHAT HAS THE COMMISSION REQUESTED IN PARAGRAPH 9.n OF

 3        THE PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST?

 4   A.   Paragraph 9.n of the Pre-Hearing Bench Request requests “A list of EPE regulatory

 5        assets or other items currently being recovered through rate riders. An explanation

 6        of whether those existing rate riders should be modified, terminated, or rolled into

 7        the rate base.”

 8

 9   Q15. IN RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.n, PROVIDE A LIST OF EPE

10        REGULATORY ASSETS OR OTHER ITEMS CURRENTLY BEING

11        RECOVERED THROUGH RATE RIDERS.

12   A.   EPE’s existing applicable riders/ rate adjustments include:

13           •   FPPCAC Rate No. 18,

14           •   EUERF Rate No. 17,

15           •   RPS Rider Rate No. 38,

16           •   AMS Rider Rate No. 46,

17           •   TEP Rider Rate No. 44, and

18           •   New Mexico Community Solar Administrative Cost Rider Rate No. 47.1.

19



                                               9
                                    Amended Filing
                            EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY
                        SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
                                MANUEL CARRASCO


 1   Q16. IN FURTHER RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.n, PROVIDE AN

 2        EXPLANATION OF WHETHER THOSE EXISTING RATE RIDERS

 3        SHOULD BE MODIFIED, TERMINATED, OR ROLLED INTO THE RATE

 4        BASE.

 5   A.   EPE proposes to roll AMS Rider Rate No. 46 costs into base rates in this

 6        proceeding, while maintaining that rate rider for costs incurred after the September

 7        2025 Test Year Period. This is explained in the Direct Testimony of EPE witness

 8        George Novela at pages 27-29.

 9                EPE proposes that the remaining riders should be maintained. Specifically,

10           •    The FPPCAC Rate No. 18 will continue to function as a flow-through

11                mechanism to recover variable fuel and purchased power costs, which are

12                not appropriate for recovery through base rates due to their volatility.

13           •    The EUERF Rate No. 17 will remain in place to recover approved energy

14                efficiency program costs to support ongoing programs consistent with

15                Commission directives.

16           •    The RPS Rider Rate No. 38 will continue to facilitate recovery of the

17                approved costs associated with compliance with Renewable Portfolio

18                Standard requirements. However, in this proceeding, EPE proposes to move

19                into base rates the Commission approved annual capacity costs related to



                                                10
                                    Amended Filing
                            EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY
                        SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
                                MANUEL CARRASCO


 1               the Santa Teresa Project Energy Storage Agreement (“ESA”) and the

2                capacity costs related to the Carne ESA. The Direct Testimony of EPE

3                witness Novela at pages 23-24 provides additional discussion including

4                EPE’s intent to also move energy costs incurred under Commission

5                approved PPAs out of the RPS Cost Rider and into its Fuel and Purchase

6                Power Cost Adjustment Clause, pending Commission approval in EPE’s

7                2026 REA Plan Case.

8            •   The TEP Rider Rate No. 44 will continue to provide recovery of costs

9                associated with EPE’s Transportation Electrification Plan, including

10               approved investments and program-related expenditures.

11           •   The New Mexico Community Solar Administrative Cost Rider Rate No.

12               47.1 will remain in place to recover administrative costs associated with

13               implementation and operation of the community solar program.

14        Accordingly, no additional modifications or terminations to EPE’s riders are

15        proposed at this time.

16

17   Q17. DOES      THIS      CONCLUDE        YOUR       SUPPLEMENTAL           DIRECT

18        TESTIMONY?

19   A.   Yes.

   DECLARATION OF MANUEL CARRASCO IN SUPPORT OF THE FOREGOING
                AMENDED FILING DIRECT TESTIMONY

       I, Manuel Carrasco, pursuant to Rule 1-011 NMRA, state as follows:

       1.      I affirm in writing under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of

New Mexico that the following statements are true and correct.

       2.      I am over 18 years of age and have personal knowledge of the facts stated herein.

I am employed by El Paso Electric Company ("EPE" or “the Company”) as the Manager of Rate

Research.

       3.      I have reviewed the foregoing Amended Filing Supplemental Testimony of Manuel

Carrasco, and the exhibits, schedules, and workpapers sponsored by me and I confirm, to the best

of my knowledge, that those materials are complete, accurate, internally consistent, and consistent

with the Amended Application.

       4.      The foregoing Amended Filing Supplemental Testimony of Manuel Carrasco,

together with all exhibits sponsored therein and attached thereto, is true and accurate based on my

knowledge and belief.

       5.      I submit this Declaration, based upon my personal knowledge and upon information

and belief, in support of EPE’s Amended Application for Revisions of Its Retail Electric Rates

Pursuant to Advice Notice No. 317.
